I have been playing with Dragonlord Ojutai quite a bit in various decks, and I often find myself trying to decide which card to keep after I get some damage through. Quite often my choice comes down to a land, some removal, and another creature. I am never to sure which is the right option though. I'm going to list a few broad scenarios. Share your opinions for each situation with me.

Scenario A: I have 5 untapped lands in play with none in my hand. I have 22 life with Ojutai and Nyx Fleece Ram on the field. In my hand is Nyx Fleece Ram, Ajani's Pridemate, and Read the Bones. The cards that are drawn Ojutai anticipates are Valorous Stance, basic land, and Brutal Hordechief. My opponent has 20 life. He has Warden of the First tree with 2 +1/+1 counters on it and Abzan Battle Priest with no counters on the board. Which card do you take?

Scenario B: 4 tapped Lands, 1 untapped white mana, Sorin Solemn Visitor, Dragonlord Ojutai, Nyx Fleece Ram on the board. My life is at 23, Opponent is at 16. Cards in my hand are Brutal Hordechief and read the bones. Opponent has Ainok Bond Kin @ 3/2, and Abzan Battle Priest @ 4/3. The Ojutai ability reveals Ajani's Pridemate, a basic land, and flooded strand.

Most of the time I end up passing on the lands and taking a removal or a creature, but I find that if the match goes long then I effectively mill all of my lands to the bottom of my deck. If I get late in the game and still have 5 or 6 mana because I milled everything, but didn't manage to finish off my opponent I'm at a huge disadvantage. When do you take land or removal for sake of the late game and when do you just go for it?
Which card to keep from Dragonlord Ojutai's anticipate?

Much of this is going to depend on your decklists, but given the information provided I'd go like this:

A: Valorous stance. Protect that Ojutai. The Anticipate ability will get you the rest of the way. B: This one is rough. There's something to be said for taking the strand to reduce lands in the deck since the Pridemate is outmatched on hitting the board. However, the Pridemate has the ability to take over the ground if you can keep him out. This is the one where the decklist will really matter.

This is roughly the decklist I'm running.

http://deckbox.org/sets/923229

The sideboard that is listed is just cards I'm thinking about including. Have a little more work to do with it, but it all seems to work together smoothly. The land base isn't what I'm actually running, but its similar.

With 24 land, if you have 5 in play and a max cost of 5 on all your cards (Secure is an x spell), I'd dump every land I could. You might want to take the lands so you can cast 2 spells per turn, but in Scenario B, you'd have to be at 7 mana - so you can offload one of those cards per turn instead anyways.
